snippet.title: How Does an F1 Crew Change Four Tires in Two Seconds?
snippet.description:
You just watched it - it was over before the question ended. So let's slow a Formula 1 pit stop down: around twenty people, three on every wheel, and three tricks hiding inside two seconds.

Trick one: one nut per wheel, dead center. Trick two: nobody ever touches that nut - it is trapped inside the wheel, so the old wheel leaves with its nut and the new one arrives with its own. Trick three: the wheel gun reverses itself - first pull off, next pull on.

A 3D engineering breakdown of the whole stop: the nose hitting the front jack before the car has stopped (powered jacks are banned - this is muscle), four nuts loose about four tenths of a second in, the one-second wheel swap, three tenths to tighten, the button every gunner presses, the green light and the driver's reaction time. Then how small the margin is: Monaco 2021, where one gun wee wheel came off 43 hours later, back at thefactory. And the record: 1.80 seconds, McLaren, 2023.

The phase times are a typical modern stop asmselves, not a frame-by-frame copy of therecord stop.

Sources:
- FIA Formula 1 Technical and Sporting Regulations (one wheel fastener per wheel; no powered device may lift the car in the pit lane; pit lane speed limit 80 km/h)
- formula1.com, "Anatomy of a pit stop" (roles, captive nut, self-reversing guns, front jack, traffic lights)
- mercedesamgf1.com, "Box, box: pitstop explpit stop perfection" (phase times, the button on the gun)
- Guinness World Records / formula1.com: fastest pit stop 1.80 s, McLaren, Lando Norris, Qatar Grand Prix, 8 October
2023
- motorsport.com, the-race.com, formula1.com on Valtteri Bottas' wheel nut at the 2021 Monaco Grand Prix

- "race driver" by BELAZ - https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/race-driver-e4e97df9865d466c8359fbb23e757308

snippet.title: O PERIGO DE CAIR DO BARCO EM ALTO MAR
snippet.description:
Cair do barco em alto mar representa um risco crítico que muitos velejadores subestimam. 

O incidente de cair do barco é uma das situações mais difíceis enfrentadas durante a navegação, especialmente quando a embarcação está em movimento. A distância que o veleiro percorre rapidamente torna o retorno ao ponto de queda extremamente difícil, exigindo manobras precisas e coordenação imediata da tripulação que permanece a bordo. Mas se estiver sozinho, exigirá muito esforço e condicionamento físico para alcançar este barco se tornando uma situação muito difícil de escapar.
A dificuldade de subir de volta ao convés é um fator determinante para a segurança marítima. Embarcações com casco mais alto criam um obstáculo físico significativo para quem está na água, muitas vezes impedindo o retorno autônomo.
